hook_text: Hang a bag on a string over a wheel and pull down. Same weight, easier job. Now hang the wheel on the bag and the weight halves.
clip_script: A pulley is a wheel with a groove, turning on an axle, with a rope in the groove. It is a wheel and axle for guiding rope. Hang it from a broom handle, 200 grams on one side, pull the other. The balance says 200. Nothing lighter, but you pulled down instead of lifting up, and the rope turned a corner with no rubbing. That is a fixed pulley. Now hang a second wheel on the load itself. Tie the string up top, down under the load's wheel, back over the fixed one, down to your hand. Pull. The balance says 100. Two ropes hold the load, each takes half, and you pull twice as far. Count the ropes holding the load: that number is your advantage. Your crane gets one light grooved wheel at the tip of the arm, so the string drops straight down to the magnet.
visual_style: Whiteboard broom handle across a doorway; cotton reel with string over it; spring balance reading 200 then 100; two rope sections highlighted; a crane arm tip with a bead pulley.
mood: Hands-on and surprised, one measurement at a time.
pacing: Wheel, hang, pull, reading, second wheel, reading, count, crane, each a beat.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and measure a pulley with a cotton reel and a bag of sand.
